title: Animation Curve Editor with Bezier Handles
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive animation curve editor with draggable bezier handles and a live 3D preview.

## Scene Setup
- Use an OrthographicCamera for the 2D curve editor panel on the left side (60% width).
- Use a PerspectiveCamera for the 3D preview panel on the right side (40% width), with a simple lit scene containing a colored sphere (radius 0.5) on a ground plane.
- The 3D scene has one directional light and one ambient light.
- Use two separate renderers or a single renderer with scissor/viewport to split the screen.
- Background: dark gray (#1a1a2e) for the curve editor, slightly lighter (#16213e) for the 3D preview.

## Curve Editor Panel (Left)
- Draw a coordinate grid with X axis representing time (0.0 to 1.0) and Y axis representing value (0.0 to 1.0).
- Render axis labels: 'Time' on X, 'Value' on Y.
- Display a cubic bezier curve defined by 4 control points: P0(0,0), P1(0.25, 0.1), P2(0.75, 0.9), P3(1,1).
- P0 and P3 are the start/end anchors (rendered as white circles, radius 8px). They are fixed on X but can be dragged on Y.
- P1 and P2 are the bezier handles (rendered as yellow circles, radius 6px). They can be dragged freely in both X and Y, but clamped to [0,1] on both axes.
- Draw thin dashed lines from P0->P1 and P2->P3 (handle lines).
- The bezier curve itself should be drawn as a smooth line (sample at least 100 points) in cyan (#00d2ff).
- When a control point is hovered, highlight it (increase radius by 2px). When dragged, change color to orange.

## 3D Preview Panel (Right)
- The sphere animates along the Y axis based on the bezier curve. The animation loops every 2 seconds.
- At normalized time t (0 to 1), evaluate the cubic bezier to get value v, then set sphere Y position to v * 4 (so range 0 to 4).
- Show a thin vertical line (pole) from ground to sphere to visualize height.
- Display current animation time and value as text overlay on the 3D panel.

## Preset Buttons (Top Bar)
- Add a top bar with 4 preset buttons: 'Linear', 'Ease In', 'Ease Out', 'Ease In-Out'.
- Linear: P1(0.25, 0.25), P2(0.75, 0.75)
- Ease In: P1(0.42, 0.0), P2(1.0, 1.0)
- Ease Out: P1(0.0, 0.0), P2(0.58, 1.0)
- Ease In-Out: P1(0.42, 0.0), P2(0.58, 1.0)
- Clicking a preset updates P1 and P2 (P0 stays (0,0), P3 stays (1,1)) and redraws the curve.

## Keyboard Controls
- Press 'Space' to pause/resume the animation.
- Press 'R' to reset all control points to default: P0(0,0), P1(0.25,0.1), P2(0.75,0.9), P3(1,1).
- Press 'T' to toggle showing/hiding the handle lines (dashed lines).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- controlPoints: array of 4 objects [{x, y}, ...] for P0, P1, P2, P3
- animationTime: current normalized time (0 to 1)
- animationValue: current bezier-evaluated value (0 to 1)
- sphereY: current sphere Y world position
- isPaused: boolean
- handleLinesVisible: boolean (default true)
- activePreset: string or null ('linear', 'easeIn', 'easeOut', 'easeInOut', null)
- selectedPointIndex: number or null (index 0-3 of currently dragged point, null if none)
- curveLength: approximate arc length of the bezier curve (sum of segment lengths from the 100+ sample points)
- loopCount: number of completed animation loops (starts at 0)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Bezier evaluation must follow standard cubic bezier formula: B(t) = (1-t)^3*P0 + 3*(1-t)^2*t*P1 + 3*(1-t)*t^2*P2 + t^3*P3. Sphere Y = bezierValue * 4. All control point coordinates clamped to [0,1]. Animation time loops every 2 seconds. Curve length must be positive and finite.
